standards.name: Minimum Information About a Peptide Array Experiment (MIAPepAE)
standards.abstract: MIAPepAE targets peptide-array experiments (primarily spotted peptide arrays, with intent to cover in situ synthesized arrays) used for protein recognition, peptide quantification and protein–protein interaction detection. The recording/data modality is array-based measurements (raw array images/signals and processed feature-level data) with associated experimental and sample metadata. MIAPepAE is a preliminary checklist-style guideline published in EMBnet.journal (2012) by Botha and Kumuthini that proposes a minimum set of data and metadata items to accompany peptide-array experiments to enable reproducibility, integration across platforms, and downstream re-use. It aligns with existing community efforts (MIAPE, MIAME, MIBBI) and emphasizes sample metadata, raw and processed data, experimental design, array annotation and protocols.

classification.rationale: The source is a prose guideline presenting a checklist of items and reporting requirements (instructions of WHAT to report) rather than a field-level table or an ordered sequence of procedural stages. The material lists objectives, high-level checklist subjects and reporting criteria (Sufficiency/Practicability), consistent with a PRINCIPLE-style standard.

principles.principle: Provide specifics to allow critical evaluation, understanding and reproduction
principles.evidence: MIAPepAE should provide authors, reviewers, editors and readers with the specifics required to critically evaluate, understand and reproduce a peptide-array experiment;

principles.principle: Provide sufficient information to enable aggregation/integration across platforms
principles.evidence: MIAPepAE should provide sufficient information to aggregate/integrate similar experimental data, independently of the platform on which the experiment was performed;

principles.principle: Enable integration of secondary data (e.g., clinical, epidemiology)
principles.evidence: MIAPepAE should allow secondary data, such as clinical patient and epidemiology data, to be integrated, enabling the extraction of more meaningful information from peptide-array experiments.

principles.principle: Include the following main checklist subjects
principles.evidence: Hence, we have drafted our checklist with the following main subjects: Raw Data, Final Processed Data for Set of Hybridisations, Sample Annotation and Experimental Factors, Experimental Design, Sufficient Annotation of Array Design, Essential Experimental and Data-Processing Protocols.

principles.principle: Adhere to the criteria of Sufficiency and Practicability
principles.evidence: We endeavour to adhere to two criteria introduced by the MIAPE article: those of Sufficiency and Practicability. Sufficiency states that the minimum information requirements are constructed in such a way that the reviewer is able to 'understand and critically evaluate the interpretation and conclusions'. The reader must also be able to support the findings. Practicability states that the incorporation of a minimum information requirement for a proteomic experiment need not be so taxing on the experimenters that its adoption is impaired.

principles.principle: Emphasize metadata pertaining to the sample
principles.evidence: We emphasise meta-data pertaining to the sample. Variation in preparation of protein/peptide samples and their assaying to the array slides can be a major contributor to experimental variation and, as such, warrants a focused effort toward the proposed guidelines.

principles.principle: Register and align with community reporting initiatives (MIBBI, MIAPE, MIAME)
principles.evidence: In the interest of coherent and coordinated development of such guidelines, the project is registered on the MIBBI porta1.

A unique peptide, as used in a peptide-array experiment, should conform to the following properties. It should have a unique identification number (ID) such as a National Centre for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) or a Protein Data Bank (PDB) number.

standards.notes: Extracted from: Botha G, Kumuthini J. Minimum Information About a Peptide Array Experiment (MIAPepAE). EMBnet.journal 2012;18(1):14-21. DOI: https://doi.org/10.14806/ej.18.1.250
